facts.statement: The genus Lectavis was named by Chiappe in 1993.
Lectavis is a genus of enantiornithine birds.
facts.quote: Lectavis is a genus of enantiornithine avialan.

facts.statement: Fossils of Lectavis were found in the Late Cretaceous Lecho Formation at estancia El Brete, Argentina.
facts.quote: Their fossil bones have been recovered from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian, c. 70.6 – 66 mya) Lecho Formation at estancia El Brete, Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Lectavis contains only one species, Lectavis bretincola.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Lectavis bretincola.

facts.statement: Lectavis bretincola had a 16 cm tibiotarsus and a tarsometatarsus that would have been nearly 10 cm long if complete.
facts.quote: L. bretincola was a sizeable bird, with a 16 cm tibiotarsus and a tarsometatarsus which if complete must have been nearly 10 cm long

facts.statement: Remains indicate that Lectavis bretincola was 41 cm long, had a hip height of 30 cm, and weighed 1.15 kg.
facts.quote: This remains indicate an animal with a length of 41 cm, hip height of 30 cm, and weight of 1.15 kg.

facts.statement: Lectavis possesses a unique hypotarsus that covers the upper end of the second toe's bones rather than the third.
facts.quote: It possesses a hypotarsus, which it evolved autapomorphically from modern birds, as it covers the upper end of the second, not the third, toe's bones.

facts.statement: The hypotarsus structure in Lectavis helps prevent the legs from shifting out of position during walking.
facts.quote: This structure serves to attach and arrest the posterior cruciate ligament, which in turn prevents the lower and upper leg from shifting out of position during walking.

facts.statement: Lectavis was an advanced enantiornithine bird, possibly related to Enantiornis and Avisaurus but likely closer to other Euenantiornithes.
facts.quote: It was a rather advanced species of enantiornithine and possibly quite closely related to Enantiornis and Avisaurus, but more likely closer to other Euenantiornithes

facts.statement: The exact evolutionary relationships of Lectavis remain unresolved.
facts.quote: Its exact relationships, as with most enantiornithine birds, are unresolved however.

facts.statement: Lectavis bretincola appears to have been a much more terrestrial species than its contemporary relative Yungavolucris brevipedalis.
facts.quote: It appears that L. bretincola was a much more terrestrial species than its relative Yungavolucris brevipedalis which lived at the same time and place.

facts.statement: Lectavis lived in a richly vegetated coastal area dotted with possibly brackish lakes or small rivers.
facts.quote: Its habitat was a richly vegetated coastal area that was dotted by – possibly brackish – lakes or small rivers

facts.statement: Lectavis belongs to the parent group Enantiornithes.
Lectavis lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
